A trait declaration contains a set of method declarations.
Syntactically, a method declaration begins with
an optional sequence of modifiers followed by
the method's name,
optional static parameters
(described in \chapref{trait-parameters}),
the value parameter with its (optionally) declared type,
an optional type of a return value,
an optional declaration of thrown checked exceptions
(discussed in \chapref{exceptions}),
an optional \KWD{where} clause
(discussed in \secref{where-clauses}),
a contract for the method (discussed in \secref{method-contracts}),
and finally an optional body expression preceded by the token \EXP{=}.
If a method declaration has the \KWD{getter} modifier,
it does not affect the behavior of a program; rather,
it documents that the method is intended to serve as a getter.
A \KWD{throws} clause does not include naked type variables.
Every element in a \KWD{throws} clause is a subtype of
\TYP{CheckedException}.


Method declarations can include the following special modifiers:
\paragraph{\KWD{getter}:}
A method declaration with the modifier \KWD{getter} explicitly declares a
getter method for a field, even in the absence of an actual field declaration.
\note{The following description is too confusing.  Reword it!!!}
If such a field exists, there is no implicit getter for the field.
An explicitly declared getter method must take no arguments and return a
result of the field's type.
A getter method must not throw any checked exception.
Getter names may not overlap ordinary method names.
A getter method must be invoked with the field access syntax:
%expr.id
\begin{Fortress}
\(\VAR{expr}.\VAR{id}\)
\end{Fortress}
where \VAR{id} is the name of the getter method.



\paragraph{\KWD{setter}:}
A method declaration with the modifier \KWD{setter} explicitly declares a
setter method for a field, even in the absence of an actual field.
\note{The following description is too confusing.  Reword it!!!}
If such a field exists, there is no implicit setter for the field.
An explicitly declared setter method must take a single argument---the
value being set---and return \EXP{()}.
A setter method must not throw any checked exception.
Setter names may not overlap ordinary method names.
A setter method must be invoked with the \emph{assignment syntax}:
%expr1.id := expr2
\begin{Fortress}
\({expr}_{1}.\VAR{id} \ASSIGN {expr}_{2}\)
\end{Fortress}


We say that a method declaration \emph{occurs} in a trait declaration.
A trait declaration \emph{declares} a method declaration that occurs
in that trait declaration.
A trait declaration \emph{inherits} method declarations from the
declarations of its immediate supertraits
except those method declarations
that are \emph{overridden} (as described later in this section) or
whose parameter type (not including the type of the self parameter)
is equal to the parameter type of a method declaration
that occurs in the trait declaration.
A trait declaration \emph{provides} the method declarations that it
declares or inherits.




There are two sorts of method declarations:
\emph{dotted method} declarations and
\emph{functional method} declarations.
Syntactically, a dotted method declaration is identical to a function
declaration.
When a method is invoked, a special self parameter is bound to the
object on which it is invoked.



A functional method declaration has a parameter named \KWD{self} at an
arbitrary position in its parameter list.  This parameter is not given a type
and implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object.
\revision{revival-self-type}{In a trait \VAR{T} with a self-type parameter \VAR{X}
(\secref{trait-decls}), this remains the type of the \KWD{self} parameter
in the declaration's signature, which overloading and the choice of a declaration
at a call read; in the method's body \KWD{self} has the type \EXP{T \cap X}
(\secref{idn-ref}).}
Semantically, functional method declarations can be viewed as top-level
function declarations.  For example, the following overloaded functional method
\VAR{f} declared within a trait declaration \VAR{A}:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.a.tex}
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.b.tex}
may be rewritten as top-level functions as follows:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.c.tex}
\input{\home/basic/examples/Trait.Method.d.tex}
where \VAR{internalF} is a freshly generated name.
Functional method declarations may be overloaded with top-level function
declarations.
An abstract function declaration
(described in \secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations})
can be provided also for overloaded functional method declarations.
See \chapref{multiple-dispatch} for a discussion of overloaded
functionals in Fortress.

When a method declaration includes a body expression, it is called a
\emph{method definition}.
A method declaration that does not have its body expression is referred to
as an \emph{abstract method declaration}.
An abstract method declaration declares an \emph{abstract method};
any object inheriting an abstract method must define a body expression for the
method: a method definition with the same name and the self parameter (if any)
at the same position whose parameter type, not counting the type of the self
parameter, is that of the abstract method declaration, or definitions whose
parameter types are subtypes of it and together cover it
(\secref{internal-types}), or it is a static error.
\revision{revival-covering}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said only that
any object inheriting an abstract method must define a body expression for the
method.
The object defines the method by a body at its parameter type, or by bodies at
narrower parameter types that together cover it, \KWD{comprises} clauses read
at the level of values (\secref{trait-decls}), as
\secref{abstractFunctionDeclarations} asks of the concrete declarations for an
abstract function declaration; one body at a narrower parameter type that does
not cover the abstract method's does not define it.
This is the rule of the type group's compiled type checker (2012) and of its
calculus Welterweight Fortress (2012).
The requirement of \secref{object-decls} that an object define all abstract
methods inherited from its supertraits is unchanged: it defines them in this
sense.}
An abstract method declaration may include the modifier \KWD{abstract}.
It may elide parameter names but parameter
types cannot be omitted except for the self parameter.


\note{
Method declarations that are overridden by some declaration are not
accessible.  They are not considered for overloading checks.

Partial overriding of an overloaded functional is allowed
but partial overriding of a functional declaration is not allowed.
}

A method declaration may have the modifier \KWD{override}.
Such a declaration \emph{overrides} any inherited declaration with the same name
and the self parameter (if any) at the same position,
whose parameter type, not counting the type of the self parameter,
is a strict subtype of the overriding declaration's parameter type.
The return type of the overriding declaration must be subtype of
that of the overridden declaration to preserve type safety.
A declaration with the modifier \KWD{override} must override
some inherited declaration.
It is a static error if a declaration with the modifier \KWD{override}
does not override any inherited declaration.

- problem: on the base `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract` was keyed on the code generator's stop, 'Likely bug in static analysis, apparently malformed overload set not rejected' (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:409-411`). The per-provider set dropped a component's own bodiless functional method (`OverloadingChecker.scala:138-141` at 528438ac5). Row 720's reproducer named the callee's result, not the call: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:411`
- spec: a trait provides what it declares or inherits, abstract declarations included (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:580-581`), and an object must define each abstract method it inherits: `Specification/basic/traits.tex:628-633`
- precedent: the team's dotted per-provider set keeps abstract dotted methods with no body filter: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:170-172`
- deviation: the team's 2012 functional set kept bodies only (a874948ac, line 133); it now keeps every functional method a type provides: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:137`
- deviation: the well-formedness walk's own `error` now chooses the error's place, with three helpers beside it and two lines of `walk`: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:42-82`
- historical: OverloadingChecker.scala, TypeWellFormedChecker.scala and `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, all of the 2012 tree: `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2622`

For where a static error is reported, the specification says nothing: `grep -rn -i 'reported at\|is reported\|location of .*error' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing.

## 1. What changed, and why

**Rows 727, 572 and 734: the per-provider check reads abstract functional methods.** Q1's answer is (a), refuse (P-149). `toFunctionalMethodArrows` now keeps every functional method a trait or object provides, as `toMethodArrows` keeps every dotted one (`OverloadingChecker.scala:131-137`). It keeps the `implemented` filter, which drops an abstract method that a declaration of a strict subtype with the same parameter types implements (`:147-152`). Before, in a component, it kept a functional method only if the method had a body or its trait came from an imported api (`:138-141` at the base). That was the judge's reading (b) of climb batch 8 (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/JUDGE.md`, section 7, decision 1). The revival's helper `declaredInUnit`, used only by that condition, is removed (`:173-181` at the base).
- Row 727: an abstract `f(self, y: S)` beside a concrete `f(self, y: S)` in one trait is refused, 'There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type: (S)'. So is the pair at two self positions, through row 707's check.
- Row 572: in `object O extends { A, B }`, `A` has an abstract `pick(self)` and `B` a concrete one. The object is refused, 'Invalid overloading of pick in trait O: A->String ... and B->String ...', as its dotted twin already was.
- Row 734, the Q1 probe's row of the same shape with return types that differ, is refused the same way.
- One more face, measured here. On the base, an object's own `f(self): String` that defines its trait's abstract `f(self): ZZ32` compiled, and its run failed with 'java.lang.VerifyError: Bad return type'. The dotted twin was refused. The return-type check of an overriding pair reads its arrows through the same function (`OverloadingChecker.scala:657-658`), so it now refuses the functional one too: 'For f, the return type of O->String ... should be a subtype of the return type of T->ZZ32'.
- Operators stay as row 584 leaves them: `isDeclaredName` and `NodeUtil.validOp` are untouched (`OverloadingChecker.scala:710-714`). A symbolic operator's pair, row 726, is still the code generator's stop.

**Row 720: a broken bound is reported at the call.** A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type. The well-formedness walk meets that type in the call's type information, and on the base it reported the error at the type node (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:158-165` at the base), which is the callee's declaration. The walk now remembers the nearest expression it is in (`:65`, `:145-146`, `:274`).
- An error on a type node that lies outside that expression is reported at the expression instead (`:47-62`, `:72-82`).
- It is reported once for each message and place of the node, as the errors at the node were. The driver drops a second error with the same text and place (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/MultipleStaticError.java:31-40`).
- It goes to the innermost expression the walk met the node in, and to the first of them where two are disjoint.
- It is not moved when the node is ill-formed where it is written: then the error stays at the declaration, as before.
- A type written inside its own expression, a parameter's type and a declaration's type keep their errors where they were.

Two earlier versions were wrong, and each fault has a test now:
- The first (96c441771) reported at the nearest expression each time. `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` printed 'has 3 errors' on it, against 1 on the base: a call in a tuple, the tuple, and a second call of the callee.
- The second (f53bee311) also moved the error of a type that is ill-formed where it is written, so that error came twice. `GenTest5` went from 32 errors to 42, and `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce` printed 'has 2 errors'.
- The third (a79a51661) gives the base's number of errors in every program I compared.

**Place.** The fix is in two places:
- the per-provider overloading check of the compiled checker (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md`, B.7), which the brief names;

- The walk checks the static arguments written at a reference where they are written (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:234-235`). A type that the reference does not write is its callee's, and its error now goes to the reference.
- The key of a moved error is the driver's own de-duplication key: the error's text and place.

The ways weighed are in section 8.

## 4. What the specification settles

Three rules refuse both rows' shapes:

- The Meet Rule for Functional Methods applies to what a type provides (`overloading.tex`, "Meet Rule"; `Specification/basic/traits.tex:580-581`). It refuses row 572's object, which provides two declarations and none on their meet.

Written 2026-09-26 by the batch's judge (first ruling, Opus), on the branch `wip/rung-wrap-operators` at `3486ad5ba`. ## 1. Ruling

**Decision: stop. The stop reaches Pavol, and my recommendation is his option (a): read the one changed output as outside the stop's purpose, as he read rung C's three (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:106`), and let the push go.**

This is the batch's own reserved stop, not a silent specification that a judge may decide. The batch record lists "a changed interpreter output in D's comparison that its step 2 does not account for" among the stops reserved for Pavol, and its section on D says of a difference the correct respelling leaves that "it is Pavol's to read ("changing no output", `POSITIONS.md:149`), not a judge's" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-5.md`, section 3, D, "Stops"). Q2 = (a) masks Java line numbers, identity hashes and library positions moved by D's lines, and nothing else (`CLIMB-BATCH-5.md` section 5, Q2; section 3, D, "No output changes", step 2). A swap of two declarations in a message is none of the three. So the worker was right to stop, and I cannot lift it. What follows is what I checked, and what I put to Pavol.

## 2. What differs, checked

- The three captures of `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInheritedOverload.fss` (`probes/count/XXXInheritedOverload.baseA.txt`, `.baseB.txt`, `.edit.txt`): base A and base B name `a(x:Sub1,y:Base)` at `:25` as "(first)" and `a(x:Base,y:Sub2)` at `:29` as "(second)"; the edit names them the other way round, and its two "more specific / less specific" lines swap with them. The exit code is 1 in all three, the two declarations are the same, and the verdict is the same: neither overload is more specific than the other.
- The file uses nothing the rung touched: two traits with one method each and an object extending both (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXInheritedOverload.fss:15-33`). No operator D declared or respelled appears in it.

## 3. The text is not a property of the program on the untouched tree

- On the base tree, with the JVM's default flags, the same file names `a(x:Sub1,y:Base)` first in 11 of 16 runs and `a(x:Base,y:Sub2)` first in 5 (`probes/order/order-repeat-base.txt`, runs 1-4 and 5-16, machine line at its head). The nine runs of `probes/order/order-probe-base.txt`, also on default flags, change order twice over k = 0..8 (at k = 3 and k = 8), where the same probe with the comparison's flags never changes (`probes/order/order-probe-base-passflags.txt`).
- Neither the launcher nor the gate pins the JVM: `grep -n 'ActiveProcessorCount\|UseSerialGC\|TieredStop'` finds nothing in `bin/fortress`, `build.xml` or `ProjectFortress/build.xml`. Only the comparison runner pins it (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/count-run.sh:20`, copied from `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-overflow/count-run.sh:18`). So the file counted as "stable" only because the comparison's three passes all ran pinned; under the flags every user and the gate run, it varies on the base already.
- In the gate it varies for one more reason: `testSystem` runs four shards in parallel, each a forked JVM with no pinning flag (`build.xml:1171-1197`, `:1206-1211`), and runs each interpreter test in-process in its shard's JVM (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:332`; `InterpreterTest`, `:708`, runs the file through `Shell` in the same JVM, `:722-729`), so the order also depends on every test that ran before it in its shard, and D's new file moves the shards' sorted order (`CLIMB-BATCH-5.md` section 4).
- The mechanism, by reading, as the worker gives it, each line opened: `FType`'s hash is a function of a global serial counter (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/types/FType.java:96-101`, returned by `hashCode` at `:88-90`); a method signature's hash is built from its domain types' hashes (`interpreter/evaluator/values/SingleFcn.java:87-95`); an object's methods are collected in a `GHashMap` keyed by that signature (`interpreter/evaluator/values/Constructor.java:181-182`) and iterated in hash order (`:325-326`); the overloading check walks the resulting list pairwise (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:229-251`) and prints the pair as "(first)" and "(second)" in list order (`:550-557`). How many `FType`s exist before `Base`, `Sub1` and `Sub2` are made therefore decides the order, and any change to the library, or to the threads that load it, can change that number.

## 4. What the gate and the specification read

- The gate reads only that the file fails. For a file whose name contains `XXX`, a thrown error is "OK Saw expected exception" unless `testFailed` objects (`FileTests.java:346-361`), and `InterpreterTest` (`:708`) does not override `testFailed`, whose base returns `null` (`:111-113`). The message text is never compared.
- The specification says when an overload set is a static error (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:80`, `:271`) and nothing about the text that reports it; the one "error message" in `Specification/basic/` is the library function `fail`'s own (`Specification/basic/tests.tex:171`). So on the point that differs the specification is silent, and the worker's home 3 for row 406 (a probe capture and a ledger row, not a gated test) is the right home, for that reason.

## 5. The worker's claims, right and wrong

Right:
- That this is the batch's stop, and that Q2 = (a) does not mask it (section 1 above).
- That every exit code is unchanged and that the base varies under default flags (sections 2 and 3; `probes/compare-normalised.txt` for the classification of the other 405 files).
- The mechanism, by reading (section 3).
- That the specification is silent on the message, so row 406 is home 3 (section 4).
- `UnsignedTest.fss`'s products are exact, so none is respelled with `DOTTIMES`: (2^16-1)(2^16+1) = 2^32-1 and (2^32-1)(2^32+1) = 2^64-1 are the maxima of `NN32` and `NN64` (`ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss:89-91`, `:194-196` at `6030e4b36`); the wrap on those lines is the right-hand `-x1`, which is respelled. Respelling an exact product would state a wrap the code does not mean, which the record forbids ("Nothing else", `CLIMB-BATCH-5.md` section 3, D, "What it rewrites").
- The declarations and their bindings: each wrapping operator right after its plain one, on `Integral` abstract and on the five types bound to new `Wrapping*` natives or, on `ZZ`, to `BigNum`'s (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:622-630`, `:664-681`, `:740-757`, `:802-819`, `:873-890`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:406-423`), the layout of the team's 2011 library (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:761-775`) and of the specification's listing (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:351-417`, read for this ruling). No declaration outside these additions changed (`git diff 6030e4b36...3486ad5ba --stat`: 18 edited files and the new test, all on the record's list).
- Deferring rows 405 and 407 rather than adding files outside the list (`CLIMB-BATCH-5.md` section 3, D, "Stops": "An edit ... to any file not named above").

Stated more strongly than measured:
- "No correct respelling removes the difference, because it comes from the added declarations themselves." Which part of the edit moves the counter was not isolated; the worker says so in its `notDone`, and 1 to 8 dummy traits or functions did not flip it under pinned flags (`probes/order/order-probe-base-passflags.txt`, `order-probe-base-passflags-fn.txt`). It does not change the ruling: the declarations and the respellings are both the decided edit, and neither touches the file. The FACTS line and row 406 in `record.md` say "rung D's added declarations flip it"; the gather should write "rung D's edit flips it".

# Rung K (`rung-checker-abstract-callsite`): the judge's ruling on its contested fix

Written 2026-10-16 by the batch's judge (Opus), on `wip/rung-checker-abstract-callsite` at `587097d58`. Nothing was built or run for it. Every point is a reading of the tree at that commit, of the worker's last code commit `a79a51661`, or of a result that the worker's `REPORT.md` or the skeptic's `SKEPTIC.md` quotes with its command.

## 1. Ruling

**`491a5631a` is upheld, and nothing is reverted. Decision: stands.** The rung lands as the branch holds it.

The skeptic contested one fix. The finding is right, and so is its way. The worker's key dropped the error of a call whose static argument breaks the bound whenever another call of the same callee, in any declaration, printed the same message. The coordinator's call 4 asks for every such call to be reported at the call. The fix reports each one, and keeps the guards that the worker built against extra errors.

## 2. What the fix changes

At `a79a51661`, a moved error was keyed on its message and on the place of the node, `n.at` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:48` at `a79a51661`). Only one error was kept per key (`:55-59` there). A second place that did not lie inside the first fell to `case _ =>` at `:59`, and was not reported.

A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type (ledger row 720). So for two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, `n.at` is the same: the callee's result type. The two calls therefore had one key and one error.

At `491a5631a`, a moved error is kept for each type node met, at the innermost expression that the walk met that node in (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:75-85`). The errors are made at the end of `check` (`:41-58`):
- If one place of a key lies strictly inside another place of the same key, the outer place gives no error (`:50-56`).
- A key that the walk also met where its node is written gives no moved error at all (`:43`, `:72-74`).

## 3. Why it is upheld

1. **Call 4 settles the place, and it settles it for each call.** Call 4 says "a static argument that breaks the callee's bound is reported at the call" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`), and the rung's section repeats it as "an error is reported at the call whose static argument breaks the bound" (`:176`).
   - The second call in `SkTwoCalls` is such a call. So is `again`'s call in the worker's own `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss:14`).
   - At `a79a51661` neither got any error. The skeptic's run (`SKEPTIC.md` section 5.2):

         tmp/.../skeptic/bin/diffrun.sh SkTwoCalls SkTwoCallsU
         SkTwoCalls.fss:9:21-29:           ... File SkTwoCalls.fss has 1 error.
         SkTwoCallsU.fss:9:21-29:  SkTwoCallsU.fss:10:22-30:  ... File SkTwoCallsU.fss has 2 errors.

   - The worker's test asserted the drop. At `a79a51661`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` held `compile_err_WIcontains=File XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss has 1 error.` (the minus line of `git show 491a5631a`).
   - Call 4's precedent is javac and scalac, which report a bound violation at each use of the type argument (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`). That is one error for each call, not one for each declaration.
   - The specification says nothing about where an error is reported (`REPORT.md`, its grep under the provenance lines). So nothing outweighs call 4 here.

2. **The worker's precedent, read exactly, gives the skeptic's answer.** The worker took its key from the driver's de-duplication (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 5; section 3, "Precedent for row 720").
   - The driver drops an error whose `toString()` it has already seen (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`).
   - That string is the place where the error is reported, followed by its description (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/StaticError.java:70-73`).
   - Once an error moves to its call, the reported place is the call's. Two calls then give two strings, and the driver keeps both.
   - The worker's key used `n.at`, the place before the move (`:48` at `a79a51661`). That is the callee's declaration, the wrong place that row 720 repairs. So the worker's key was not the driver's key. It carried the base's wrong place into the de-duplication.

3. **A printed name does not identify a type variable across declarations.**
   - With the worker's key, whether `second`'s call is reported depends on whether `second` calls its parameter `T` or `U` (`SkTwoCalls` against `SkTwoCallsU`, above).
   - The tree's own test of the same principle, for bound checks, is `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/BoundCheckSameNameTwoScopes.fss:1` and `:11-12`: "the same question about T has two answers". That test is the revival's (`3c67d5204`), not the team's.

4. **The fix meets each of the worker's concerns.**
   - *A call inside a tuple was counted twice in the first version* (`REPORT.md` section 1, "The first (96c441771)"). The call's place lies inside the tuple's, so only the call's place is kept (`:50-56`). `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` now asserts two errors: one at the call in the tuple, at `:13:21-`, and `again`'s own. It does not assert three.
   - *A type that is ill-formed where it is written was counted twice in the second version.* `written` suppresses every moved place of that key (`:43`, `:72-74`). `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce.test` still asserts 'has 1 error'.
   - *A type built twice from one declaration* (decision 5's way not taken). One call's own expressions nest or coincide. Nested places keep the inner one. Coinciding places print the same string, which the driver drops (`MultipleStaticError.java:34-37`).
   - *A call's value that flows to a later use.* The use shares the call's node, so it adds no place (`:79-85`). Fix 5.1 makes the walk meet the call first (`:286-287`, upheld as settled in `SKEPTIC.md` 5.1).
   - The skeptic's runs on `491a5631a`: the rung's 35 test files, 'OK (47 tests)'; `ant testQuick`, 'Tests run: 1222, Failures: 0, Errors: 0', 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL' (`SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.2 and 11).

5. **The library's sites hold by reading.**
   - The rung's section says that row 720's repair "moves two sites without adding one" (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, rung K, "Distance sites").
   - `MaxSumReductionPair` and `MinSumReductionPair` appear in `Library/` only at their declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3405`, `:3411`) and at one call each (`:3422`, `:3424`). So each moved key has one place, and the fix gives one error for each, as the worker's code did.
   - The skeptic's instrumented runs agree on the tables' api rows and on the two moved sites (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Row 488").

## 4. Each side's claims

**The worker was right that:**
- the first version multiplied errors (`REPORT.md` section 1);
- the driver de-duplicates on text and place (`MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`);
- a key on node identity alone would double one call's type wherever it is built twice. The skeptic agrees, and that is why the nesting rule exists (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Mine").

**The worker was wrong that** "each of the base's distinct errors stays one error" is a requirement. No decision on record asks for the base's count of errors outside the library.
- The base's single error for two calls came from its wrong place (point 2 above).
- `GenTest5` rises from 32 to 36 errors, at the four `cross` calls at `:645-648` and a second reference at `:384`, with its first error unchanged (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Its cost"). Each new error is a call that call 4 asks to be reported. `GenTest5` is outside the suites (`ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/`).

**The skeptic was right** about the defect, its dependence on another declaration's parameter name, and call 4's reading (points 1 to 3 above).

**The skeptic measured less than it implied.** Three things in section 5 below are not measured on the committed fix. None changes the ruling.

## 5. What lands unmeasured or unrepaired: for the gather and the curator

1. **No count stage or distance stage ran on `491a5631a`** (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2 and 11).
   - The skeptic's instrumented count run with this code lost row 488's site at `FortressLibrary.fss:130` ('#total 38', '#locations 37'). The worker's file, compiled the same way, did not.
   - The mechanism was not found. The symptom is the one F-232 records: two instrumented runs that shifted the JVM's identity-hash sequence lost `:130` (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:282-283`, `:350`).
   - Rung H makes the checker's output the same under any identity-hash sequence. Call 3 names `:130` going or staying as H's own cost (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, call 3).
   - So the gate on the merged tree is the first measure of this fix. If the gate's count or distance moves at any site other than `:130` and the two moved sites `:3422` and `:3424`, the gather looks at `491a5631a` first.
   - `record.md:22` ("In the library no error is added or dropped: the count stays 39 and the distance 49") holds for this fix by reading only (point 5 above). The gather takes the numbers from the gate.
2. **P-148's time for this fix is not measured.**
   - The walk is 0.7 % of the count stage's samples (`REPORT.md:148-149`).
   - The fix adds a linear scan for each moved error (`:79-80`), and a scan over each key's places at the end (`:45-56`). In the library each key has one place (point 5 above).
   - The gate's count stage times the merged tree.
3. **A line of `record.md` is stale.** The handover line "A call's ill-formed type is reported at the call, once." (`record.md:53`) should read "once for each call", as `record.md:19` and `:32` already do. This is the gather's correction.
4. **A residual case, found by reading and not reproduced.**
   - Take two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, where one call is an argument of the other, such as `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))` with a bounded `next`. Both calls' types have one key. The inner call's place lies inside the outer's, so the outer call gives no error (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:50-56`).
   - This case is narrower than the defect fixed, and it does not depend on any other declaration. The program is still refused, at the inner call.
   - The worker's way (e) closes it in general: a call's type takes the call's spans (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 3). It changes the spans that every message prints, so it is not this batch's.
   - If a later rung reproduces the case, it gets a ledger row.

## 6. If call 4 is reversed

Call 4 is the coordinator's, listed for the curator's review and reversible (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, "The coordinator's calls this batch builds"). If the curator reads "at the call" as "once per callee", `git revert 491a5631a` removes the fix together with its test, the rekey and its lines of `record.md`. The dropped call then needs a ledger row at home 3, with `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` as its reproducer (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, last paragraph).

At `a79a51661`, a moved error was keyed on its message and on the place of the node, `n.at` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:48` at `a79a51661`). Only one error was kept per key (`:55-59` there). A second place that did not lie inside the first fell to `case _ =>` at `:59`, and was not reported.

A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type (ledger row 720). So for two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, `n.at` is the same: the callee's result type. The two calls therefore had one key and one error.

At `491a5631a`, a moved error is kept for each type node met, at the innermost expression that the walk met that node in (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:75-85`). The errors are made at the end of `check` (`:41-58`):
- If one place of a key lies strictly inside another place of the same key, the outer place gives no error (`:50-56`).
- A key that the walk also met where its node is written gives no moved error at all (`:43`, `:72-74`).

## 3. Why it is upheld

1. **Call 4 settles the place, and it settles it for each call.** Call 4 says "a static argument that breaks the callee's bound is reported at the call" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`), and the rung's section repeats it as "an error is reported at the call whose static argument breaks the bound" (`:176`).
   - The second call in `SkTwoCalls` is such a call. So is `again`'s call in the worker's own `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss:14`).
   - At `a79a51661` neither got any error. The skeptic's run (`SKEPTIC.md` section 5.2):

         tmp/.../skeptic/bin/diffrun.sh SkTwoCalls SkTwoCallsU
         SkTwoCalls.fss:9:21-29:           ... File SkTwoCalls.fss has 1 error.
         SkTwoCallsU.fss:9:21-29:  SkTwoCallsU.fss:10:22-30:  ... File SkTwoCallsU.fss has 2 errors.

   - The worker's test asserted the drop. At `a79a51661`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` held `compile_err_WIcontains=File XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss has 1 error.` (the minus line of `git show 491a5631a`).
   - Call 4's precedent is javac and scalac, which report a bound violation at each use of the type argument (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`). That is one error for each call, not one for each declaration.
   - The specification says nothing about where an error is reported (`REPORT.md`, its grep under the provenance lines). So nothing outweighs call 4 here.

2. **The worker's precedent, read exactly, gives the skeptic's answer.** The worker took its key from the driver's de-duplication (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 5; section 3, "Precedent for row 720").
   - The driver drops an error whose `toString()` it has already seen (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`).
   - That string is the place where the error is reported, followed by its description (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/StaticError.java:70-73`).
   - Once an error moves to its call, the reported place is the call's. Two calls then give two strings, and the driver keeps both.
   - The worker's key used `n.at`, the place before the move (`:48` at `a79a51661`). That is the callee's declaration, the wrong place that row 720 repairs. So the worker's key was not the driver's key. It carried the base's wrong place into the de-duplication.

3. **A printed name does not identify a type variable across declarations.**
   - With the worker's key, whether `second`'s call is reported depends on whether `second` calls its parameter `T` or `U` (`SkTwoCalls` against `SkTwoCallsU`, above).
   - The tree's own test of the same principle, for bound checks, is `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/BoundCheckSameNameTwoScopes.fss:1` and `:11-12`: "the same question about T has two answers". That test is the revival's (`3c67d5204`), not the team's.

4. **The fix meets each of the worker's concerns.**
   - *A call inside a tuple was counted twice in the first version* (`REPORT.md` section 1, "The first (96c441771)"). The call's place lies inside the tuple's, so only the call's place is kept (`:50-56`). `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` now asserts two errors: one at the call in the tuple, at `:13:21-`, and `again`'s own. It does not assert three.
   - *A type that is ill-formed where it is written was counted twice in the second version.* `written` suppresses every moved place of that key (`:43`, `:72-74`). `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce.test` still asserts 'has 1 error'.
   - *A type built twice from one declaration* (decision 5's way not taken). One call's own expressions nest or coincide. Nested places keep the inner one. Coinciding places print the same string, which the driver drops (`MultipleStaticError.java:34-37`).
   - *A call's value that flows to a later use.* The use shares the call's node, so it adds no place (`:79-85`). Fix 5.1 makes the walk meet the call first (`:286-287`, upheld as settled in `SKEPTIC.md` 5.1).
   - The skeptic's runs on `491a5631a`: the rung's 35 test files, 'OK (47 tests)'; `ant testQuick`, 'Tests run: 1222, Failures: 0, Errors: 0', 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL' (`SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.2 and 11).

5. **The library's sites hold by reading.**
   - The rung's section says that row 720's repair "moves two sites without adding one" (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, rung K, "Distance sites").
   - `MaxSumReductionPair` and `MinSumReductionPair` appear in `Library/` only at their declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3405`, `:3411`) and at one call each (`:3422`, `:3424`). So each moved key has one place, and the fix gives one error for each, as the worker's code did.
   - The skeptic's instrumented runs agree on the tables' api rows and on the two moved sites (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Row 488").

## 4. Each side's claims

**The worker was right that:**
- the first version multiplied errors (`REPORT.md` section 1);
- the driver de-duplicates on text and place (`MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`);
- a key on node identity alone would double one call's type wherever it is built twice. The skeptic agrees, and that is why the nesting rule exists (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Mine").

**The worker was wrong that** "each of the base's distinct errors stays one error" is a requirement. No decision on record asks for the base's count of errors outside the library.
- The base's single error for two calls came from its wrong place (point 2 above).
- `GenTest5` rises from 32 to 36 errors, at the four `cross` calls at `:645-648` and a second reference at `:384`, with its first error unchanged (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Its cost"). Each new error is a call that call 4 asks to be reported. `GenTest5` is outside the suites (`ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/`).

**The skeptic was right** about the defect, its dependence on another declaration's parameter name, and call 4's reading (points 1 to 3 above).

**The skeptic measured less than it implied.** Three things in section 5 below are not measured on the committed fix. None changes the ruling.

## 5. What lands unmeasured or unrepaired: for the gather and the curator

1. **No count stage or distance stage ran on `491a5631a`** (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2 and 11).
   - The skeptic's instrumented count run with this code lost row 488's site at `FortressLibrary.fss:130` ('#total 38', '#locations 37'). The worker's file, compiled the same way, did not.
   - The mechanism was not found. The symptom is the one F-232 records: two instrumented runs that shifted the JVM's identity-hash sequence lost `:130` (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:282-283`, `:350`).
   - Rung H makes the checker's output the same under any identity-hash sequence. Call 3 names `:130` going or staying as H's own cost (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, call 3).
   - So the gate on the merged tree is the first measure of this fix. If the gate's count or distance moves at any site other than `:130` and the two moved sites `:3422` and `:3424`, the gather looks at `491a5631a` first.
   - `record.md:22` ("In the library no error is added or dropped: the count stays 39 and the distance 49") holds for this fix by reading only (point 5 above). The gather takes the numbers from the gate.
2. **P-148's time for this fix is not measured.**
   - The walk is 0.7 % of the count stage's samples (`REPORT.md:148-149`).
   - The fix adds a linear scan for each moved error (`:79-80`), and a scan over each key's places at the end (`:45-56`). In the library each key has one place (point 5 above).
   - The gate's count stage times the merged tree.
3. **A line of `record.md` is stale.** The handover line "A call's ill-formed type is reported at the call, once." (`record.md:53`) should read "once for each call", as `record.md:19` and `:32` already do. This is the gather's correction.
4. **A residual case, found by reading and not reproduced.**
   - Take two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, where one call is an argument of the other, such as `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))` with a bounded `next`. Both calls' types have one key. The inner call's place lies inside the outer's, so the outer call gives no error (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:50-56`).
   - This case is narrower than the defect fixed, and it does not depend on any other declaration. The program is still refused, at the inner call.
   - The worker's way (e) closes it in general: a call's type takes the call's spans (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 3). It changes the spans that every message prints, so it is not this batch's.
   - If a later rung reproduces the case, it gets a ledger row.

## 6. If call 4 is reversed

Call 4 is the coordinator's, listed for the curator's review and reversible (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, "The coordinator's calls this batch builds"). If the curator reads "at the call" as "once per callee", `git revert 491a5631a` removes the fix together with its test, the rekey and its lines of `record.md`. The dropped call then needs a ledger row at home 3, with `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` as its reproducer (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, last paragraph).

input.ruling:
I uphold 491a5631a and revert nothing.

**The skeptic was right on three points.**
- **The defect is real.** At a79a51661 a moved error was keyed on its message and the node's place before the move, n.at (TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:48 at a79a51661). Only one place was kept per key, and a second place that did not lie inside the first fell to `case _ =>` (:59 there). Two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike share n.at, which is the callee's declared result (ledger row 720). So the second call got no error. SKEPTIC.md 5.2: 'SkTwoCalls.fss:9:21-29: ... File SkTwoCalls.fss has 1 error.' against 'SkTwoCallsU.fss:9:21-29: SkTwoCallsU.fss:10:22-30: ... has 2 errors.' The worker's own XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test asserted 'has 1 error'. That means `again`'s call at XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss:14 was reported nowhere.
- **Call 4 settles it for each call.** Call 4 says the error 'is reported at the call' (CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84), and the rung's section repeats it (:176). It cites javac and scalac, which report at each use. The specification is silent on where an error is reported (REPORT.md's grep).
- **The key made the report depend on another declaration's parameter name.** A printed name does not identify a type variable across scopes. The tree's own BoundCheckSameNameTwoScopes.fss:1 and :11-12 rest on the same principle; that test is the revival's, 3c67d5204.

**The worker was right that:**
- the first version multiplied errors (REPORT.md section 1);
- the driver de-duplicates on text and place (MultipleStaticError.java:31-39);
- node identity alone would double a type that is built twice for one call.

**The worker was wrong that its key is the driver's key.**
- The driver's key is the reported error's toString(), which is the reported place followed by the description (StaticError.java:70-73). After the move, that place is the call's place, so the driver itself keeps two calls apart.
- The worker's key kept the base's wrong place.
- No decision on record asks for the base's error count outside the library. GenTest5 rises from 32 to 36 errors, and each new error is a call or reference that call 4 asks to be reported.

**The fix meets each of the worker's concerns.**
- Nested places of one key keep the inner one (TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:50-56).
- A key whose node is ill-formed where it is written moves nothing (:44, :72-74).
- A later use shares the call's node and adds no error (:79-85). Fix 5.1 makes the walk meet the call first (:286-287).
- The library's two moved sites have one call each (FortressLibrary.fss:3422, :3424), so they are unchanged by reading.
- The skeptic's runs on 491a5631a: 'OK (47 tests)', and testQuick 'Tests run: 1222, Failures: 0'.

**The skeptic measured less than it implied.** No count or distance stage ran on the committed fix. Its instrumented count run lost row 488's :130, the symptom F-232 records (perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:282-283, :350). The fix's time under P-148 was not measured. Both are left to the gate on the merged tree (JUDGE.md section 5).
